agents-middleware.summary: In LangChain 1.x, `create_agent` (from `langchain.agents`) is the standard agent: a model calling tools in a loop, compiled to a LangGraph graph. You customise it with middleware hooks rather than new agent classes. Know the hook order, which built-in middleware solves which production problem, how structured output and human approval work inside the loop, and how legacy `AgentExecutor` code maps onto it.
points: `create_agent(model, tools, *, system_prompt, middleware, response_format, state_schema, context_schema, checkpointer, store, ...)` returns a compiled graph. The loop alternates a `model` node and a `tools` node, and it ends when the model replies with no tool calls. A `return_direct` tool, a graceful limit or a `jump_to: "end"` also end it.

Node-style hooks (`before_agent`, `before_model`, `after_model`, `after_agent`) return state updates. Wrap-style hooks (`wrap_model_call`, `wrap_tool_call`) receive a `handler` and can retry, short-circuit, or rewrite the call via `request.override(model=..., tools=..., messages=..., system_message=...)`.

Ordering for `middleware=[m1, m2, m3]`: `before_*` hooks run m1 to m3, `wrap_*` hooks nest with m1 outermost, and `after_*` hooks run m3 to m1. `before_agent` and `after_agent` run once per invocation; model hooks run on every model call.

Use a decorator (`@before_model`, `@wrap_model_call`, `@dynamic_prompt`, ...) for a single quick hook. Use an `AgentMiddleware` subclass for several hooks, sync and async variants, configuration, a `state_schema` of its own, or extra `tools` that ship with the middleware.
Jumps: a node hook returns `{"jump_to": "end" | "model" | "tools"}` and must declare the target with `can_jump_to` (`@hook_config(can_jump_to=[...])` or the decorator argument).

Request overrides in `wrap_model_call` affect only that call. State updates from node hooks are persisted by the checkpointer. The system prompt is applied at call time and is not stored in `messages`.

Built-ins: `SummarizationMiddleware` (needs a `trigger`; `keep` defaults to 20 messages), `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`, `ModelCallLimitMiddleware` (`run_limit`/`thread_limit`, exit `end` by default), `ToolCallLimitMiddleware` (exit `continue` by default), `ModelFallbackMiddleware`, `ModelRetryMiddleware`/`ToolRetryMiddleware`, `PIIMiddleware`, `LLMToolSelectorMiddleware`, `ContextEditingMiddleware`, `TodoListMiddleware` (adds `write_todos`).

`response_format`: `ToolStrategy` (the schema becomes an artificial tool; supports unions; `handle_errors=True` retries on validation errors) or `ProviderStrategy` (provider-native, optional `strict`). A bare schema picks the provider strategy when the model profile supports it. The result is in `result["structured_response"]`.

Human in the loop: `interrupt_on={"tool": True | False | {"allowed_decisions": [...]}}`, with decisions approve, edit, reject or respond. It needs a checkpointer and a `thread_id`, and you resume with `Command(resume={"decisions": [...]})`, one decision per action in order.

Runtime context: declare `context_schema`, pass `invoke(..., context=...)`, and read `runtime.context` in node hooks, `request.runtime.context` in wrap hooks, or a hidden `ToolRuntime` parameter in tools.

Migration: `langgraph.prebuilt.create_react_agent` became `create_agent` and `prompt` became `system_prompt`. Pre and post model hooks became `before_model`/`after_model`, dynamic models and tool error handling moved to `wrap_model_call`/`wrap_tool_call`, custom state must be a `TypedDict` extending `AgentState`, and `AgentExecutor`/`initialize_agent` live in `langchain-classic`.

Positioning: LangGraph is the runtime, LangChain's `create_agent` is a minimal harness, and Deep Agents is an opinionated harness built on it (filesystem, subagents, skills). Use a plain chain or graph when the steps are fixed.
traps: An exception raised inside a tool body propagates and fails the run by default. Only invalid arguments and unknown tool names become error `ToolMessage`s automatically, so add `wrap_tool_call` or retry/error middleware.
Returning `jump_to` without declaring `can_jump_to` is silently ignored: the model step still runs.
A sync-only `wrap_model_call` raises `NotImplementedError` under `ainvoke`/`astream` (and async-only fails under `invoke`). Sync node hooks still work in async runs.
Two instances of the same middleware class fail the build as duplicates. Configure one `ModelCallLimitMiddleware` with both `run_limit` and `thread_limit`.
`PIIMiddleware` checks only user input by default. Set `apply_to_tool_results` and `apply_to_output` to catch data that enters through tools or leaves in replies.
`HumanInTheLoopMiddleware` without a checkpointer can still pause, but the resume fails. Also, `respond` tells the model the tool succeeded, so use `reject` to deny an action.
Adding tools in `wrap_model_call` that were never registered with `create_agent` raises an error when the model calls them, unless a `wrap_tool_call` executes them.
